source.title: Sequences of cognitive decline in typical Alzheimer's disease and posterior cortical atrophy estimated using a novel event-based model of disease progression.

confidence_rationale: Directly instruments the object INV-047 asserts -- the fine-grained ORDER in which cognitive deficits appear -- using a data-driven event-based model that requires no a priori clinical staging. Strongly supports the claim's structural half (decline is staged and syndrome-specific, not uniform: PCA is vision-first, typical AD is memory-first). Weakens the claim's specific ordering, because the recovered typical-AD sequence begins with memory, not with the precision/confidence stage INV-047 places first. Confidence reflects a well-matched measurement returning a partially discordant answer.
failure_signatures: The recovered sequence for typical AD is MEMORY-first. INV-047 places precision/confidence loss before episodic memory failure. On the one dataset that models the ordering directly, the claim's first two stages appear in the opposite order.

The neuropsychological battery covers memory, vision, arithmetic and general cognition -- it contains no metacognitive or confidence measure at all. The absence of a confidence-first stage in the recovered sequence is therefore uninformative about whether one exists: the model cannot order an event it never measured.

Two syndromes with the same underlying proteinopathy yield different cognitive orderings (PCA vision-first vs tAD memory-first), which shows the ordering is set by lesion topography rather than by any single canonical dependency sequence -- a challenge to INV-047's derivation of the order from a phase-dependency structure.

mapping.source_claim_statement: An event-based model adapted for highly non-Gaussian cognitive test data recovers fine-grained sequences of cognitive decline that differ between posterior cortical atrophy (vision first) and typical Alzheimer's disease (memory first).
mapping.ree_translation: INV-047 asserts a specific staged ordering of cognitive failure. This is the methodological instrument that can adjudicate such orderings from data, and it confirms the claim's underlying premise: decline follows a recoverable, phenotype-specific sequence rather than uniform degradation. Its recovered ordering for typical AD constrains INV-047's stage list -- episodic memory appears at the front, where INV-047 places precision/confidence.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The discordance must NOT be read as refutation. The battery (memory, vision, arithmetic, general cognition) contains no metacognitive or confidence instrument, so a confidence-first stage could not have been recovered even if it were present -- this is a measurement gap, not a negative finding. Additionally the model orders test-score abnormality events, which are downstream composites, not the underlying functional channels INV-047 is about; and 'contextual identity loss' / 'global disorientation' have no corresponding events in this battery either.
mapping.source_context: Clinically-diagnosed PCA and typical AD patients at the UCL Dementia Research Centre; cross-sectional neuropsychological battery; event-based model with nonparametric mixture modelling to handle ceiling/floor effects.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality methods paper in a top dementia journal, and unusually well matched to the claim's form (it models orderings, which is what INV-047 asserts). Mapping fidelity discounted because the battery cannot see three of INV-047's four stages, so the comparison is only partial and the apparent conflict is weaker than it looks.
